The Sartell mill began operations with a No. 1 paper machine in September 1905 and added No. 2 in 1910 [d6550336s1p0].
The mill produced newsprint until 1930 and then converted to groundwood book and magazine papers [d6550336s1p0].
The mill implemented deinking and bleaching of recycled magazines in cookers during the 1930s recycling operations [d6550336s1p0].
The Sartell mill closed its finishing operation after World War II and thereafter shipped all paper in roll form [d6550336s1p0].
Reed established a newsprint manufacturing operation at Tovil Mill in 1895, indicating adoption of newsprint production technology at that site [d420576s2p0].

sub_answers.text: The Sartell mill began operations with No. 1 paper machine in September 1905 and added No. 2 paper machine in 1910 [d6550336s1p0]. The mill produced newsprint until 1930 and then converted to groundwood book and magazine paper production, indicating adoption of mechanical groundwood pulping technologies for those grades [d6550336s1p0][d215844s2p0]. During the 1930s the mill operated a conversion plant that performed deinking and bleaching on recycled magazines in cookers, indicating implementation of deinking and bleaching processes for recycled-fiber feedstock [d6550336s1p0]. After World War II the mill closed its finishing (sheeting and cutting) operation and thereafter shipped all paper in roll form, reflecting a change in finishing/process flow at the mill [d6550336s1p0].

sub_answers.text: The Sartell mill sourced large volumes of recycled magazines transported by rail from Chicago in the 1930s for pulping and deinking operations [d6550336s1p0]. The original company founders were lumbermen and the mill’s early operations used log drives on the Mississippi River as a timber transport method [d6550336s1p0]. The plant also experimented with nonwood raw materials such as corn stalks, indicating diversification of raw-material inputs during its early decades [d6550336s1p0].

sub_answers.text: The Watab Pulp and Paper company was formed in 1905 with a stated capitalization and stock structure, reflecting corporate formation and governance arrangements at startup [d6550336s1p0]. The company made an agreement to move an existing sawmill into Sartell for $1.00, demonstrating a strategic reorganization of local assets to the new mill site [d6550336s1p0]. At the end of World War II the mill closed its finishing operation and reorganized distribution to ship all paper in roll form, reflecting an operational consolidation decision implemented after the war [d6550336s1p0].

sub_answers.text: No. 2 paper machine was built in 1910 at the Sartell plant, representing an early capital expansion of production capacity [d6550336s1p0]. The mill converted from newsprint to groundwood book and magazine paper production in 1930, representing a major programmatic change of production scope [d6550336s1p0]. During the 1930s the mill operated a conversion plant for deinking and bleaching recycled magazines and kept that conversion plant operating through the 1930s until the end of World War II, representing a sustained capitalized processing capability [d6550336s1p0]. The mill closed its finishing operation after World War II, altering installed-capacity utilization and downstream equipment use by shipping only rolls thereafter [d6550336s1p0].
